source_title: We need to win the trust of our fans again, says new MI batting coach Uthappa - Sportstar
source_excerpt:
Uthappa had also played for Mumbai Indians during the inaugural edition. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri
Five-time champion Mumbai Indians finished ninth in the IPL 2026 season, and newly-appointed batting coach Robin Uthappa is well aware that the franchise under head coach Kieron Pollard will have to make amends this time.
“Today, we find ourselves back in that similar situation where the trust of the fans need to be earned again. We come in again as underdogs. it’s been one full cycle, and we’re back to where we started again, which is nice,” Uthappa said in an interview to franchise’s website.
He said MI must become as feared a side on the road as it is when playing at the Wankhede Stadium.
“We’re a force to reckon with at home. I want to take that same emotion, that same energy to every venue away from home. My goal would be to make sure that that sense of intimidation that teams feel when they come to Mumbai Indians, to the Paltan, I want them to feel that same intimidation when we go away from home as well.
“I’m looking forward to playing a part in that journey of earning the fans’ trust back and making sure that this underdog journey will be one to be remembered.”
To rediscover MI’s glory days, Uthappa said he would work with the domestic players to empower them and make them confident.
“I would love to empower domestic cricketers and help them get clarity. That’s one of the most important aspects that the young cricketers need at this point in time, clarity of what they want to do, how they want to do it, and what is the process by which they’re going to achieve those aspects.
“You’re also emotionally investing in their own journey, and then you’re rooting for them. You want them to do well. And so when they do well, it feels like a personal achievement.”
Recollecting his own experience, he said, “I remember when one of the lads I was working with and mentoring got picked up in the Indian Test squad, it felt like I got selected. It felt that emotional.
“That’s something that I’m looking forward to, especially with domestic cricketers. And communication is a big part of it, and those are conversations I’m genuinely looking forward to.”
Uthappa described his appointment as Mumbai Indians batting coach as “destiny” as he had started his IPL career with the franchise in 2008. As part of MI’s squad in the first IPL season in 2008, Uthappa scored 320 runs from 14 matches at an average of 35.55 and a strike rate of 114.69.
“I am just genuinely happy to be back ... thrilled about this and delighted to have this opportunity to work with this special set of cricketers and this franchise,” Uthappa said in a video uploaded by MI on the franchise’s social media handle.
Sachin Tendulkar and Robin Uthapa during a practice session during IPL 2008. | Photo Credit: S. Subramanium
“Incredible, and it just feels like destiny, to be honest. As in, I started my IPL career with Mumbai Indians and I start my IPL coaching career with Mumbai Indians, which seems like destiny to me.”
He also recalled the excitement he felt when he came to know that he was picked by MI and would be in the same team as batting legend Sachin Tendulkar in the inaugural edition.
“Back in 2008, when I got into the franchise, I remember we were in Australia, playing the CB Series when the auctions happened, and I knew that I was going to be playing with my hero, Sachin paaji over here.
“So for me, that was really exciting feeling, because everyone was finding their feet in that first season, and including the franchises and players and teams, and the IPL itself. We had, I would say, a fairly decent season, could have been better.
“We had injuries, and paaji (Sachin Tendulkar) missed a big part of that tournament, and then Bhajju pa (Harbhajan Singh) captained as well, and Sanath (Jayasuriya) played really well, Polly (Shaun Pollock) played really well.”
Uthappa turned out for six IPL franchises in his career and won the title with Kolkata Knight Riders in 2014 and Chennai Super Kings in 2021, and finished with 4,952 runs from 205 IPL matches.
